text:
harper: Quick heads-up — packaging ran into a manifest split while assembling the sealed offline bundle for v1.9.2-private. Two submanifests (A and B) have different signer fingerprints. Need a decision before our Fri 02:00 UTC delivery window.

maria: Ugh. Is this from a late artifact republish or signer rotation?

harper: Looks like a republish. Build system picked up an old signer for chunk-B. `sha256` mismatch in chunk manifest index. I pasted the snippet below.

harper: ```
chunk-A: signer=redwood-signer-v3 (sha256:aa11...ff)
chunk-B: signer=redwood-signer-v2 (sha256:bb22...ee)
expected: signer=redwood-signer-v3
```

simon: If we proceed with mixed-signers customers can't validate with single-key pinning. That will break offline verification.

olivia: Is there a fast remediation? Re-sign chunk-B with v3? Who holds the v3 private key for airgap signing today?

harper: Ops has the v3 key in the HSM, but re-signing requires a new cosign step and republish. It'll push the deliverable by ~45m.

jen: We have a canary customer waiting. If we delay, can we ship a dual-key verified bundle and document the extra key in release notes? (Not ideal for pinned installs.)

simon: Dual-key adds support burden and some customers refuse multi-key trust. I'd prefer re-sign and keep single-key pin.

maria: Agree with simon. Is there a rollback impact window? If we re-sign, do we need to bump the epoch/manifest id? Our transport expects immutable manifest IDs.

harper: Re-sign will update manifest checksum, so yes epoch bump. We'll need to pin the new epoch in deploybot and update the `install-manifest` TTL.

deploy-bot: @harper To proceed with re-sign, run `!deploybot package-resign --manifest chunk-B --signer v3 --epoch bump` in #release-runner. This will create a new artifact and schedule a staging canary.

harper: Doing it now. I'll post the new checksums once done. ETA ~25m.

olivia: Heads-up — maintenance window in EU transport at 02:15 UTC overlaps our delivery. If we push, transport might be slower.

jen: If transport is flaky, we should plan a fallback: deliver delta bundle plus a signed TTLed redirect so customers can fetch the bumped manifest after maintenance. Document in release notes.

simon: OK plan: (1) re-sign chunk-B with v3, (2) bump epoch, (3) run a staging canary for 20m, (4) if canary OK — proceed to full airgap package publish; else rollback to previous sealed bundle and hold window. Everyone good with that?

maria: +1

olivia: +1 (will open a quick transport watch during the push)

harper: New artifact published. New epoch `epoch-2026-03-21-1`. Checksums:

harper: ```
sealed-bundle-v1.9.2-epoch-2026-03-21-1.tar.gz sha256: cc33...aa
chunk-B re-signed signer=redwood-signer-v3 sha256: dd44...bb
```

deploy-bot: @harper staging canary started (id: canary-3187654321-1). Will report health in 15m.

jen: Preparing release notes snippet for private customers: call out reason (republish signer mismatch), that we re-signed, epoch bumped, and rollback criteria.

harper: Canary healthy at 12m. No verification errors in staging.

simon: Good. Proceeding to full publish now. I'll update the transport monitors and pin the new epoch in the release manifest.

deploy-bot: publish job queued by simon. ETA rollout ~10m. If any host failures exceed 2% in 5m window, automatic rollback to previous epoch will trigger.

olivia: Transport slow but within SLOs. Monitoring tail latency.

jen: Release notes drafted and uploaded to the release docs repo under `private-releases/v1.9.2-notes.md` with a clear rollback procedure and contact points.

harper: Rollforward complete. All customers' bundles show new epoch and verify with v3 key. Closing thread and adding a note to the canary dashboard.

simon: Thanks everyone. Postmortem: add a pre-publish signer-check step to packaging pipeline to avoid future mixed-signers.

maria: Agreed — I'll add the CI gate.

harper: :thumbsup:
